defects_found.description: capture-worker crashes with WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT (compute exhaustion) on at least 2 distinct large PDFs even under v1.6 — the invocation is killed mid-processing, no agent_runs/pending_first_fetch write occurs, and the claimed row is left stuck at status='fetching' regardless of how recently it was claimed (the 1-hour stale-reset rule does not catch a same-session crash).
defects_found.root_cause: [HYPOTHESIS, unverified this session — outbound curl to downloads.regulations.gov was blocked by the container's egress allowlist, so the actual PDF byte size/page count could not be checked] v1.6's readCappedBody pre-buffer size guard bounds bytes READ against MAX_PDF_BYTES (25MB), but does not bound the compute cost of pdf.js parsing (getDocumentProxy/extractText) itself once a PDF is under the byte cap. v1.6's own source comment already names this as a known residual risk ('pdf.js parsing... is the expensive step on the PDF path, so 25MB is already a heavy in-memory parse'). The crash most likely occurs during parsing, not buffering, since neither row shows a BodyTooLargeError-style refusal.

defects_found.description: The HTTP/2 'stream error received: unexpected internal error encountered' class (12 rows, 10 of 12 on *.gov.au domains sharing an IPv6 prefix family, plus fred.stlouisfed.org and pollution-waste.canada.ca) persists identically under v1.6, confirming run-002's hypothesis that this is a connection-layer/client-compatibility defect, not a timing issue AbortSignal.timeout could touch.
defects_found.root_cause: [HYPOTHESIS, carried forward from fetch-drain-run-002.json, not newly investigated this session] Plausibly Deno's fetch client (rust hyper/reqwest) failing to negotiate or fall back cleanly against a CDN/edge configuration common to these hosts.
